text:
I need to tell our staff that we're ending fully remote work. I'm one of the three partners at an architecture firm with 46 architects and designers.

What I can say:
- From September 1, everyone works in the office on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
- 15 of our people were hired as fully remote in 2021 and 2022. 4 of them live more than two hours from the office.
- Those 4 can keep working remotely until the end of next year. After that, they come in once a week.
- Last year we lost two large hospital projects in the final interview. Both clients told us our team seemed not to know each other.
- Based on our review records, junior staff hired since 2022 are taking about 30% longer to reach the point where they lead a project.
- The partners have been coming in one day a week. We'll be in all three days too.

Keep it to one page. It goes out by email before an all-staff meeting on Friday.

Before I write this, I need a few answers. Here is the argument I plan to make. Correct anything that's wrong.

- **Decision:** From September 1, everyone works in the office Tuesday to Thursday. The partners will be in all three days too.
- **Evidence:** You lost two hospital projects at final interview because the team "seemed not to know each other." Juniors hired since 2022 are taking about 30% longer to reach project lead.
- **The reasoning that connects them:** Our work depends on a team that clients can see works together, and on juniors learning by watching seniors work. Both need us in the same room on the same days.
- **What people will object to:** The 15 people hired as fully remote will see this as changing the terms they joined on. 11 of them get no exception at all. People will also say the partners are asking for something they haven't been doing themselves. Your last fact answers that one, so the email will open with it rather than hide it.

**Questions:**

1. **Which September 1?** Today is November 16, so I'm reading this as September 1, 2027. In that case the 4 long-distance staff stay remote until December 31, 2027, and come in one day a week from January 2028. Is that right? That gap is long enough that people will ask about it.
2. **What do the other 11 remote hires get?** They will read this email harder than anyone else. Is anything being offered to them, such as help with commuting costs, a gradual start, or a fair way to leave if they can't do it? Is remote work written into their contracts? If there's nothing, I'll say plainly that the partners will talk to each of them individually, but only if that's actually going to happen.
3. **What if someone has a reason they can't come in?** Is there a way to ask for an exception for caregiving or health? And are Mondays and Fridays still remote, or up to each person?
4. **Will the office days be different from a normal desk day?** For example, mentoring set up for juniors, team reviews, or interview rehearsals held on those days. Also, does the office have room for 46 people at once? Staff will ask both.
5. **Who signs it, and when is the meeting?** Is it from you or all three partners? What time is the meeting on Friday, and should the email invite questions in advance?
6. **Is there anything staff remember or will find out?** For example, did the firm ever say remote work was permanent when it hired those 15 people? If so, the email should address that directly.

Once I have your answers, I'll write the one-page email.

1. Yes, September 1, 2027. The 4 stay remote until end of 2027, then once a week from January 2028.
2. We'll pay up to $150 a month toward commuting for anyone who lives more than 30 miles away. I don't know whether remote work is in their contracts. I can't commit to individual talks, and no exceptions beyond the 4.
3. No exceptions beyond those 4. I don't know about Mondays and Fridays.
4. I don't know about the office days. We don't have a desk for everyone yet. New desks arrive in August.
5. From me, Paul Whitaker. The meeting is Friday at 10 a.m. in the main studio. Questions before it can go to me or to HR.
6. I don't know.

<final_document>
Subject: Working in the office from September 1, 2027

Everyone,

From September 1, 2027, everyone at the firm will work in the office on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. That includes the three partners. We have been coming in one day a week, and we will be in all three days with you.

I know this is a real change, especially for the 15 of you who joined in 2021 and 2022 as fully remote. You took those jobs on terms that suited your lives, and we are changing those terms. That is not a small thing, and I won't pretend it is. Here is why we have decided to do it.

Last year we lost two large hospital projects at the final interview. Both clients told us the same thing: our team seemed not to know each other. Our work was good enough to reach the final round. What cost us the projects was how we came across as a team. A client handing us a hospital wants to see a team that already works well together, and they could see we didn't.

The second reason is how our junior staff are developing. Our review records show that juniors hired since 2022 are taking about 30% longer to reach the point where they lead a project. Much of what gets someone ready to lead is picked up by working near people who already lead: hearing how a hard client call is handled, watching a drawing set get marked up, asking a quick question instead of waiting for a meeting. That is hard to learn through a screen, and our newer colleagues are paying for it in their careers.

What this means in practice:

- From September 1, 2027, everyone works in the office Tuesday to Thursday.
- The four colleagues who live more than two hours from the office will keep working remotely until the end of 2027. From January 2028, they will come in one day a week.
- There will be no other exceptions.
- Anyone who lives more than 30 miles from the office can claim up to $150 a month toward commuting costs.
- We don't have a desk for everyone yet. New desks arrive in August, before the change starts.

We are telling you now, more than nine months ahead, so that anyone who needs to change childcare, travel or other arrangements has time to do it.

I will go through all of this at the all-staff meeting on Friday at 10 a.m. in the main studio. If you would like to raise something before then, send it to me or to HR.

Paul Whitaker
</final_document>

I left out three things you didn't have answers for. You may want to settle them before Friday:

- **Mondays and Fridays.** I didn't say whether these stay remote. It will probably be the first question at the meeting, so it's worth deciding beforehand.
- **Contracts.** Before this goes out, have HR check whether remote work is written into any of the 15 contracts. If it is, this email changes contract terms and may need to be handled differently.
- **"No other exceptions."** I included it because you said it. In many places, though, employers have a legal duty to consider reasonable accommodations, for example for a disability. Check with HR or your employment lawyer that this line doesn't commit you to something you can't hold to.
